name: Musée National du Bardo
funding: State museum. A 2001 World Bank loan (~24M TND, plus 9.5M TND from the state) paid for the 2009-12 expansion; a 2017 Louvre partnership was backed by TOTAL Tunisie, Loukil, ATUGE and Dar El Marsa.
watch: Tunisia's largest museum, known for its Roman mosaics; closed July 2021 to Sept 2023.
records_note: The museum's website did not load, so its reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked.

name: Musée National des Beaux-Arts d'Alger
watch: About 8,000 works, from Delacroix and Monet to Baya and Racim; reopened after its 2020 COVID closure.
records_note: The museum's old site posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board; it is a state establishment under the culture minister.

name: Montresso Art Foundation (Jardin Rouge)
watch: Residency on a 10-hectare olive grove 20 km outside Marrakech, hosting about 40 artists a year; visits by appointment.
records_note: The foundation's site posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board; it names only collaborating institutions and its Amis de Jardin Rouge association.

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Medellín (MAMM)
funding: Mid-size private museum founded 1978; pillars are Medellín city hall, national Culture Ministry, Comfama, SURA, Bancolombia, EPM, Fundación Fraternidad and Fundación MUV.
watch: Roster read on its own Pilares y aliados page. Public utility EPM is a pillar; Celsia (an energy firm) is credited for website support.
records_note: The museum posts annual reports for 2022 to 2025, 2024 financial statements, a named list of pillars and allies, and its 12-member board.

name: Museo Nacional de Etnografía y Folklore (MUSEF)
funding: State museum (60 years in 2022) funded through the Fundación Cultural del Banco Central de Bolivia, a public body under the central bank.
watch: Holds more than 33,000 cultural objects. Its director was pushed out in 2020 after a change of government and reinstated in 2021.
records_note: MUSEF has no records of its own; parent Fundación Cultural del BCB posts reports 2019 to 2025, statements 2018 to 2025 and its council.

name: Museo Nacional del Ecuador (MuNa)
funding: State national museum; the government has budgeted about US$100M for a new building, with a state-owned enterprise managing construction.
watch: The government overturned the jury's choice of design for the new building in July 2026.
records_note: The museum's site and its ministry's site both block automated access, so nothing could be checked.

name: Museo de Arte Costarricense (MAC)
funding: Ministry of Culture museum with a 2021 budget of about COLONES 1.77bn (about US$3M), 48% of it salaries; about 37,000 visitors in 2018.
watch: Public collection museum in La Sabana. Its board approved lending works to the presidential offices in Sep 2026 without saying which works.
records_note: The MAC posts leadership reports for 2018 to 2022, budget and execution reports, and board minutes, but no funder list or board roster.

name: Museo Nacional de Arte Moderno Carlos Mérida (MUNAM)
funding: State museum of the Ministerio de Cultura y Deportes, which spent over Q16M (about US$2M) on roof and museography works in 2023-25.
watch: Closed since Nov 2022, with no reopening date as of Oct 2025.
records_note: The museum has only a page on its ministry's site with no reports, funders or board; the ministry posts budget execution for the whole ministry.

name: Fundación Casa de los Tres Mundos
funding: Small cultural foundation built with German, Austrian, Swiss and Dutch government grants and the City of Granada; closed by the Nicaraguan state in 2024.
watch: Founded 1987-89 by Ernesto Cardenal and Dietmar Schönherr. Ran art and music schools and Radio Volcán.
records_note: The foundation's archive site names its 2022 board but posts no annual reports, accounts or funder list; closed in 2024.

name: Museo Popol Vuh
funding: Small university museum of Universidad Francisco Marroquín, supported by corporate room sponsorships; the last roster published is for 2019.
watch: Pre-Hispanic and colonial collection. The sponsors page (edited Dec 2025) still lists 2019 sponsors: Pepsi/CBC, Pollo Campero and CMI.
records_note: The museum has no records of its own; its parent university posts audited statements and annual reports, and its sponsor page shows three 2019 logos.

name: Museo Larco
watch: Pre-Columbian collection. Led by president and CEO Andrés Álvarez Calderón Larco.
records_note: Larco publishes no annual reports, accounts or sponsors; its directory names only an executive president and a director, not a board.

name: Siida Sámi Museum (Saamelaismuseo Siida)
funding: A small state-backed museum: most of its money comes from Finland's Ministry of Education and Culture, plus a yearly grant from Inari Municipality.
watch: Owned by the Sámi Museum Foundation, whose board must be at least half Sámi. Its exhibition renewal was paid for by Finnish foundations.
records_note: Siida's site posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board names; it says only that the foundation board has eight members.
